chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Attar narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Oramah, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Harun, from al-Mufaddal, from al-Sa'd al-Kaffaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The hearts are four: a heart in which there is hypocrisy and faith, a capsized heart, a sealed heart, and a blooming, luminous heart. I asked: What is the blooming one? He said: It is like the lamp. As for the sealed one, it is the heart of the hypocrite. As for the blooming one, it is the heart of the believer; if God grants him gratitude, he is grateful, and if He tests him, he is patient. As for the capsized one, it is the heart of the polytheist.
Then he recited this verse: 'Is one who falls prostrate on his face better guided or one who walks upright on a straight path?'

As for the heart that has faith and hypocrisy, they are a people who were in Ta'if. If the death of one of them overtakes him while he is in a state of hypocrisy, he perishes; and if it overtakes him while he is in a state of faith, he is saved.

key_terms.قَلْبٌ أَزْهَرُ أَنُورٌ: Blooming, luminous heart (the heart of the true believer)
key_terms.قَلْبٌ مَطْبُوعٌ: Sealed heart (one where good and evil struggle, dominated by the stronger)
key_terms.قَلْبٌ مَنْكُوسٌ: Capsized heart (one that does not comprehend or accept truth)
key_terms.قَوْمٌ كَانُوا بِالطَّائِفِ: The people of Ta'if (exemplars of the mixed heart)

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of hearts in Shia theology and how is the mixed heart described?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates four spiritual states of the heart, linking the 'capsized' (mankus) to polytheists and the 'sealed' (matbu') to hypocrites, while describing the 'blooming' (azhar) heart as that of the believer who maintains gratitude and patience. The 'mixed' heart, containing both faith and hypocrisy, is exemplified by the people of Ta'if, whose final destiny hinges on the state prevailing at the time of death. This classification underscores the dynamic nature of faith in Shia theology, where the heart's condition is not always static but subject to change until the final moment.

en.basel-kadem: 50.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said:

Hearts are (of) three (types): a capsized heart that does not comprehend anything of goodness, and that is the heart of a disbeliever; a heart in which there is a black mark, and so, good and evil are wrestling in it, and that which is the strongest will dominate it; and an open heart in which there is a lamp that radiates and whose light is not extinguished until the Day of Resurrection, and that is the heart of a believer.
